short_description: Stacking cases, bags or trays onto a pallet at the end of a production line, to a pattern and at line rate.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: A box on a conveyor is the friendliest object in manufacturing: known geometry, known pose, known rate. Vendors quote guaranteed case rates, dozens of integrators compete, and cobot palletizers have pushed the price down to where a single line can justify one. Nothing here is a research question; the argument is footprint and price.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale; mixed-SKU pattern building is the remaining frontier
regress_criteria: A shift to packaging formats that defeat vacuum and clamp tooling

incumbent_process.text: Operators lifting cases off a conveyor onto a pallet by hand, or a fixed mechanical layer palletizer built for one pattern.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Manual palletizing is among the highest injury-rate jobs in a plant, and the mechanical alternative cannot change pattern without retooling — which is why the robot displaced both.

approaches.short_description: A collaborative arm on a wheeled base or lift column, moved between lines and set up by an operator rather than an integrator.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Packaged cobot palletizers are sold by every cobot vendor and several specialists, and small manufacturers buy them precisely because there is no integration project. They stay a step behind the fixed cell because payload and reach cap the case rate, so they win the low-volume line and lose the high one. Scaling rather than mature until they take share on the fast lines too.
advance_criteria: Cobot palletizers quoted at case rates competitive with fixed cells
Operators reconfiguring patterns without vendor support as the norm
Repeat purchases across multiple lines at the same plant
regress_criteria: Payload and speed limits proving a hard ceiling, confining these to demonstration lines

approaches.short_description: A dedicated arm at the end of a line stacking cases or bags to a pattern, usually with a vacuum or clamp tool.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: End-of-line palletizing is the single most standardised robot application in existence: the part geometry is a box, the pattern is software, and the vendors sell it as a configured product with a quoted rate. Buyers argue about price and footprint, not feasibility.
advance_criteria: Already at the top of the scale; watch mixed-SKU pattern building as the next frontier

technical_requirements.text: Tooling that holds the actual package

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Vacuum works on a sealed case and fails on a shrink-wrapped bundle or a bag; the end effector, not the arm, decides whether a given plant's product can be palletized at all.
advance_criteria: Would be relaxed by tooling that spans case, bag and tray without a change.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Single-SKU patterns are solved. Building a stable mixed pallet from an arbitrary order is a packing problem plus a stability problem, and it is where the remaining engineering sits.
advance_criteria: Would be satisfied by mixed-case pallets built at rate without human correction.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: High case volumes, hard washdown environments and severe manual-handling injury exposure make this the densest palletizing buyer.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Consumer goods lines run continuously with stable case formats, which is the best possible fit for a fixed palletizing cell.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Marketing changes the pack format and the tooling stops working. The cell's lifetime is tied to a package design decision that the plant does not control.
advance_criteria: Tooling changes handled in-house within a shift
Cells requalified for a new pack format without vendor engineering

blockers.text: Floor space at the end of the line

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Plants were laid out before the cell existed, and the end of the line is the most congested place in the building. This is the single most common reason a justified palletizer does not get installed.
advance_criteria: Cells with a footprint small enough to drop in without moving the line
Vendors quoting installation without a plant layout change

economics_notes.text: Payback is usually argued on injury and turnover as much as on headcount, because manual case stacking carries some of the highest recordable injury rates in a plant.

assessment.author: editorial
assessment.rationale: Plants that only count hourly wages undervalue the cell; the insurance and absence line is often the larger number, though it varies enough by employer that it should not be quoted as a rule.
advance_criteria: Would firm up with published customer injury-rate data before and after installation.
